source.stem:
The diagram shows a bar magnet at rest on a smooth horizontal surface. A length of soft-iron wire is held parallel to the magnet.
The wire is released.
What happens?

options.text: The wire moves away from the magnet.
The wire moves towards the magnet.
The wire’s centre stays in its present position and the wire rotates through 90 ° in a clockwise direction.
The wire’s centre stays in its present position and the wire rotates through 90 ° in an anticlockwise direction.

mx.teacher_note: Only the stars forming the familiar figure belong to the constellation.

mx.name: surface_feature_capture
mx.teacher_note: Solid connecting lines are real lines in the sky; dotted connecting lines are imaginary.

intelligence.enrichment: Stars shine with their own light, while groups of stars may only appear to form familiar patterns; constellations are regions of the sky that include such apparent patterns, and the connecting lines are imaginary aids for identification. Imaginary connecting lines help the eye recognize a pattern, and defined sky regions give that pattern a constellation name. The learner correctly applies this rule: Stars shine with their own light, while groups of stars may only appear to form familiar patterns; constellations are regions of the sky that include such apparent patterns, and the connecting lines are imaginary aids for identification. The lines drawn between stars are really in the sky, so a constellation is the outlined picture.
